newsitem.title: USA: FORECAST-U.S. HMO margins seen pressured in Q3, Q4.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-U.S. HMO margins seen pressured in Q3, Q4.

text.p: Profit margins are under pressure across the HMO industry and analysts see few signs of a let-up with quarterly financial results around the corner.
U.S. health maintenance organizations are locked into premium levels that are not keeping pace with unexpectedly high medical cost inflation this year, analysts said.
"That has sort of cooked their goose. Nobody has had a major turnaround," said Volpe Welty HMOs analyst Ed Keaney.
Wall Street estimates for six of the 10 largest HMOs project negative earning comparisons versus a year ago.
Showing gains on the quarter will likely be Oxford Health Plans, United Wisconsin Services, PacifiCare Health Systems and FHP International, which is being acquired by Pacificare, analysts said.
Companies that disappointed in the second quarter will likely do so through 1996, analysts said.

"All the fundamentals that were there in the second quarter are still there, as far as struggling to recover from a mismatch between premiums coming in and costs," said Vector Securities HMOs analysts John Kreger.
Meantime, the industry continues to consolidate.
The past six months have seen three mega-deals -- Foundation Health -Health Systems International, Pacificare-FHP, Aetna -U.S. Healthcare -- and dozens of smaller mergers and acquisitions.

The cost-control imperative is driving much of the consolidation, as are broadly lower stock values and continued inter-marriage among old-style indemnity insurers and managed healthcare firms, analysts said.
